description.narrative: Air quality is a multi-sectoral, long-term challenge in BiH that will require concerted actions by different stakeholders across the different levels of government of BiH over many years or even decades. Reducing air pollutant emissions and mitigating the negative impacts on welfare requires investment programs as well as policy and regulatory measures.The proposed project can be viewed as an incubator of air quality improvement coordination and actions in BiH, that will strengthen air quality management and monitoring and contribute to lowering air pollution through investments in sustainable heating and energy efficiency in single-family houses and low-emission transport. This first air quality project with World Bank support in this area in BiH is proposed with the following components. Component 1: Strengthening Air Quality Monitoring and Management. This component will focus on improving the operation of the air quality monitoring network in selected cantons of the FBiH and the sectoral capacity to estimate pollution levels and use collected data to improve planning of air quality management.Component 2: Scaling Up Sustainable Heating and Energy Efficiency in Residential Houses. This component will contribute to reducing emissions from heating of residentials houses by providing grants for cleaner heating solutions and energy efficiency investments. Component 3: Supporting the Transition to Low-Emission Transport. This component will pilot the transition to low-emission transport in the Sarajevo canton by developing cycling infrastructure, incl. monitoring and information systems, as well as acquiring low-emission public transport vehicles and providing technical assistance to support the transition to low-emission transport in the urban core.Component 4: Project Implementation Support. This component will finance project implementation activities, such as the cost of project management and implementation consultants, equipment, logistics, studies and capacity building.

The Project Development Objectives (PDOs) are to strengthen air quality monitoring and management and reduce air pollutant emissions from the residential heating and transport sectors in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

condition.narrative: Not later than three (3) months from Effective Date, the Borrower shall cause the Project Implementing Entity, through FMoET, to:(i) purchase and install a Financial Management (FM) software for accounting; and (ii) establish a Project Grievance Mechanism.

The Borrower shall cause the Project Implementing Entity: (a) through FMoF, to enter into a sub-agreement (the “Sub-Agreement”)with the Participating Cantons stipulating the financial obligations of the Participating Cantons; (b) under Parts 1 and 2 of theProject, through FMoET, to enter into an agreement or other adequate arrangement (the “Agreement of Understanding”) with eachParticipating Canton, through its cantonal government, under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank including inter alia (i)the technical implementation arrangements and role of MoE PITs to provide technical support to FMoET PMU to carrying out of theProject; and (ii) the Participating Canton's obligation to comply with this Agreement, the Project Agreement and the ProjectManuals;(c) under Part 3 of the Project, through FMoET, to enter into a memorandum of understanding (“MoU”) with the CantonSarajevo, through its Ministry of Traffic, under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank, including inter alia (i) thetechnical implementation arrangements and role of MoT PIT to provide technical support to FMoET PMU to carrying out the Project;(ii) the MoT obligation to provide technical support to FMoET PMU to carry out the Project activities in accordance with thisAgreement, the Project Agreement and the POM.
